clue.text: Cutting Republican settles in bar

indicators.note: to settle in somewhere is to make a home inside it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: bar as a preposition means apart from
R is the standard abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A cost-cutting Republican politician props up a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting' reads as an adjective for the Republican, but it is the noun: R goes inside EXCEPT to make EXCERPT.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutting is a passage clipped from a newspaper, and an excerpt is likewise an extract taken from a longer text.

clue.text: Object to circular letter you and I had funded

blocks.note: an object is an aim or goal, an end
the round letter
you and I had contracts to we'd

explanation.surface: Someone objects to a round-robin letter about a project the two of them paid for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object to' looks like a verb of complaint; Object is the noun END, and to just joins it to the next piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow an institution is to give it a permanent income, so an endowed body has been funded.

clue.text: On tour in cab lost-in busy sprawl

indicators.note: letters that are lost have wandered from their places and must be found in a new order

blocks.note: the eleven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A tourist in a taxi has lost their way in a crowded, sprawling city.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen joining lost and in is a quirk of the printed text; lost signals the shuffle and in links it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A conurbation is an extended urban area where towns have merged, exactly a busy built-up sprawl.

clue.text: Strenuous part of schooling in genuine reverse

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the word that follows

blocks.note: genuine means real
PE is physical education, the energetic school subject

explanation.surface: A strenuous school lesson really does go backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverse' wants to be a reversal signal, but nothing is turned around: it is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeal a law is to revoke or undo it, which is to reverse an earlier decision.

clue.text: Luvvie’s dreadful art screened by ethical cast

definitions.note: a noun; a theatrical is a stage person

indicators.note: something dreadful is a mess, so these three letters are jumbled
cast in the sense of thrown about scatters the letters into new places
something screened is hidden behind or within a surrounding cover

blocks.note: seven letters to rearrange around the others
three letters, themselves rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor's terrible performance is hidden by a cast of high principles.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate shuffles are needed, one wrapped inside the other. A luvvie is British slang for a gushing, self-regarding actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatrical, as a noun, is a professional actor, and luvvie is the affectionate British slang for exactly that kind of stage person.

clue.text: On leaving, wife’s child at university is promoted

indicators.note: the word named as leaving departs, removed from the piece it was in

blocks.note: the letters to remove
a wife's son by an earlier marriage is her husband's stepson
to be up is to be in residence at university

explanation.surface: On going off to university, the wife's son wins promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On leaving' reads as a time phrase, as in on going away, but it is an instruction to drop those two letters. Being up at university is a British idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who steps up moves to a higher post or level of responsibility, which is being promoted.

clue.text: Shilling’s down for a local packed lunch

blocks.note: s was the abbreviation for the old British shilling coin
nap is the soft raised surface of cloth, like down

explanation.surface: A shilling has been put down to pay for a local's packed lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' reads as being set down, but it is the fluffy pile on fabric. Snap is northern English dialect for a packed lunch, hence local.
explanation.definitionFit: In parts of northern England, snap is the miner's or worker's word for food taken to work in a tin.

clue.text: English and American spies in second waste

indicators.note: in puts the spies inside the word that follows

blocks.note: the usual abbreviation
a mate is a second in command on a ship
the US intelligence agency

explanation.surface: British and American agents squander a second.
explanation.walkthrough: The spies go inside the word for second, not between the other pieces. 'waste' is a verb here, as in wasting away.
explanation.definitionFit: To emaciate is to make thin and feeble, the sense of waste in wasting away from illness or hunger.

clue.text: Asian gentleman is not half ready

indicators.note: not half asks for a word with half of its letters taken away

blocks.note: is contracts to 's
fruit that is ready to eat is ripe

explanation.surface: An Asian gentleman is far from ready.
explanation.walkthrough: Not half sounds like the British slang for very much indeed, but here it removes the back half of RIPE. Sri is an Indian title of respect.
explanation.definitionFit: Sri is an honorific placed before a man's name in India and Sri Lanka, the equivalent of Mr.

clue.text: Spread outside a pub like The Feathers?

indicators.note: outside wraps the first piece around the one after it

blocks.note: pâté is a paste spread on toast
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: Pâté is served outside a pub called The Feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Feathers is a common British pub name, which hides the definition: the question mark flags that the feathers themselves are meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinnate describes a leaf or structure shaped like a feather, with parts arranged on either side of a central axis.

clue.text: Get into fleece before the start of November

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, here taken to follow the first piece

blocks.note: to do someone is to swindle or fleece them
its first letter

explanation.surface: Pull on a fleece before November arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: The fleece looks like a garment to put on, which suits the definition, but it is the verb meaning cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: To don a garment is to put it on, which is to get into it.

clue.text: Power with Praetorian shifts in readiness

indicators.note: shifts moves the letters about into a new order

blocks.note: P is the symbol for power
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Praetorian Guard, the Roman emperor's bodyguard, works its shifts ready to wield power.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in preparation means doing it in readiness, the state of being prepared.

clue.text: Contest bombast then question out loud a pledge

indicators.note: out loud means the word is to be heard rather than read

blocks.note: a war is a contest of arms
a rant is bombastic speech
the question word why, heard as the letter

explanation.surface: A debate full of hot air, then a promise questioned openly.
explanation.definitionFit: A warranty is a written guarantee, a pledge that goods will be repaired or replaced if faulty.

clue.text: Key people in charge of returning pictures

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the whole run is read backwards

blocks.note: A is a musical key
men are people
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: The key figures running a gallery bring back the paintings.
explanation.walkthrough: The pictures sound like artworks, but in British usage the pictures is the cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: Going to the pictures is the British idiom for going to the cinema, the place where films are shown.

clue.text: Liberating force led in close to Stepney Green

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is taken
liberated letters are set free to move into a new order

blocks.note: ten letters to rearrange
its last letter joins the mix

explanation.surface: A liberating army marches in near Stepney Green, a district of East London.
explanation.walkthrough: Stepney Green is a real London place name, so Green looks welded to Stepney; it is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Green in the environmental sense describes anything that does little harm to nature, which is what eco-friendly means.

clue.text: Held in place odd thing to produce tattoo

blocks.note: kettling is the police tactic of penning a crowd in one spot
rum is British slang for odd

explanation.surface: An odd object, fixed in position, is used to make a tattoo.
explanation.walkthrough: The tattoo sounds like ink on skin; it is a drumbeat, as in a military tattoo.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo is a rapid rhythmic drumming, and a kettledrum or timpani is a large drum that can beat one out.

clue.text: Tie’s liable to fray on Democrat

indicators.note: on means placed after, so this piece follows the next one

blocks.note: the usual abbreviation
a raw edge of cloth is unhemmed and frays

explanation.surface: A Democrat politician's tie is getting tatty.
explanation.walkthrough: The tie looks like neckwear, which fits fraying; it is a drawn game.
explanation.definitionFit: A draw is a contest that ends level, with neither side winning, the sporting sense of a tie.

clue.text: Item on menu? None merits being served another way

indicators.note: a dish served another way is presented differently, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A diner grumbles that no dish on the menu deserves to be served differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Minestrone is a thick Italian vegetable soup, a common starter listed on restaurant menus.

clue.text: Italian lady’s leader leaves part of Bible unread

indicators.note: when the leader leaves, the first letter goes

blocks.note: signora is Italian for a married lady
NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: An Italian lady's guide abandons part of the Bible without reading it.
explanation.definitionFit: Unread can describe a person who has read little, uneducated and lacking knowledge, hence ignorant.

clue.text: Small ruler faces loads of restorative procedures

indicators.note: to face something is to stand in front of it, so this piece comes first

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a king rules
a raft of things is a large number of them

explanation.surface: A minor monarch undergoes a great many treatments.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin grafts transplant healthy skin over burns or wounds, surgery that restores damaged tissue.

clue.text: Sneak about school houses: she has no handicap

indicators.note: a building houses whatever lives inside it

blocks.note: a rat is an informer or sneak
c for circa, about
SCH is the abbreviation for school

explanation.surface: A sneak hangs around school houses, said of a pupil with no disadvantage.
explanation.walkthrough: Handicap here is golf's: a scratch player plays off zero, with no strokes given.
explanation.definitionFit: A scratch golfer has a handicap of zero, so she receives no handicap allowance.

clue.text: A crush needs unending restraint

indicators.note: unending means without its end, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: a cramp is a clamp, and to cramp is to restrict

explanation.surface: A schoolchild's infatuation calls for some self-control that never ends.
explanation.walkthrough: Crush suggests infatuation, but it is a crowd squeezed together, a cram.
explanation.definitionFit: A cram is a tightly packed crowd, the same thing as a crush of people squeezed into a space.

clue.text: Slander surrounding gallery changed

indicators.note: surrounding places the first piece all round the second

blocks.note: to sling mud is to slander
the Tate is the London art gallery

explanation.surface: Smears about an art gallery have shifted.
explanation.definitionFit: To mutate is to undergo change in form or nature, so mutated means altered.

clue.text: Dupe a visitor to Trafalgar Square

blocks.note: first meaning: a gullible person who is easily cheated
second meaning: the bird famously flocking in that London square

explanation.walkthrough: The visitor sounds like a tourist being cheated, but it is the bird; Trafalgar Square in London was long famous for its flocks.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigeon is slang for a gull or easy mark, and also the bird that crowds Trafalgar Square.

clue.text: Deliverance? Half of answer’s in short Biblical book

indicators.note: half of a word keeps just one of its two halves
in places this piece inside the book's short form

blocks.note: Rom is the short form of Romans
its first three letters, half of six

explanation.surface: Seeking deliverance, someone finds half the answer in a book of the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: A ransom is a price paid to free a captive, and in religious language the redemption that brings deliverance.

clue.text: Rueful writer I provided with cover

indicators.note: provided with means given something extra, which here is added on the end

blocks.note: a pen writes
taken as written
a tent is a canvas cover

explanation.surface: A writer regrets taking shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: Penitent means feeling sorry for wrongdoing, and rueful means regretful, so both describe remorse.

clue.text: It leaves white, unknown part of natural drink

indicators.note: the word named as leaving is taken out of what follows

blocks.note: the letters removed
taken as written
y is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: An unknown ingredient leaves a natural drink white.
explanation.walkthrough: The natural drink is milk, which separates into curds and whey.
explanation.definitionFit: Whey is the watery liquid left when milk curdles, one of the two parts it separates into.

clue.text: Damaging program the Greeks aggressively piled out of

definitions.text: the Greeks aggressively piled out of

blocks.note: first meaning: malicious software disguised as something harmless

blocks.clueFragment: the Greeks aggressively piled out of
blocks.note: second meaning: the wooden horse at Troy, from which hidden soldiers poured to attack

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one sentence about a computer program, but it falls into two halves: modern malware and the legend of Troy.
explanation.definitionFit: Malware hidden inside innocent-looking software is named after the hollow horse the Greeks used to smuggle soldiers into Troy.

clue.text: S American’s source of nutrition in avocado

indicators.note: in points to letters sitting inside the next word

blocks.note: the letters in its middle

explanation.surface: A South American gets their nourishment from avocados.
explanation.walkthrough: Avocado fits the scene as South American food, so it looks like the definition; it only holds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Oca is a tuber grown in the Andes, a staple root vegetable that has fed South Americans for centuries.

clue.text: What I must have when small but not you?

definitions.text: What I must have when small but not you?

blocks.clueFragment: What I must have when small
blocks.note: surface reading: what I needed as a child, unlike you
setter's reading: the lower-case letter i bears a mark above it that lower-case u lacks

explanation.walkthrough: I and you read as people, but they are the letters i and u; small means lower case.
explanation.definitionFit: The tittle on a lower-case i is a little point, which the letter u never carries.

clue.text: Well! Virtuous type becomes husband in secret

indicators.note: becomes says one piece turns into another, swapping it out

blocks.note: stealthy means done in secret
ST, saint, is the virtuous type to replace
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Goodness! A saint turns into a secret husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well!' looks like an exclamation of surprise; it is the adjective meaning in good health.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well means being in good health, which is what healthy describes.

clue.text: At start of week, looked flush

blocks.note: MON is the calendar abbreviation for Monday
to eye something is to look at it

explanation.surface: On Monday morning someone looked red in the face.
explanation.walkthrough: Flush suggests blushing, but it is the slang sense of having plenty of money.
explanation.definitionFit: To be flush is to have money to spare, and moneyed means wealthy.
